T09.1.title: Add the editor and the block schema with ids (with T09.2)
T09.1.what:
Add the Tiptap editor as a React component with permanent block ids, plus the flat task block and the standard text marks. Built **together with T09.2 (#32) in one pull request**; the pull request says `Closes #31, closes #32`. Tiptap 3 and React Flow are already installed (#144). Add no dependencies; if something is missing, build the rest and describe it under **Decision needed**. No reading or writing files here (T10 does that), and the date chip, table, slash menu, drag handle and links are not part of this.

## Brief

**Where:** new folder `src/editor/`. Pure logic stays free of React so it tests without a browser; there is no DOM test library in the repo, so do not add one.
- `blocks.ts`: `BLOCK_TYPES`, the single list of block-level node names that carry an id: `paragraph`, `heading` (levels 1 and 2 only), `bulletList`, `orderedList`, `listItem`, `taskBlock`, `codeBlock`, `blockquote`. A table (and its row and cell nodes) is added later with T13a because it needs another dependency.
- `extensions.ts`: the extension list. `StarterKit` with the pieces this phase does not use turned off (horizontal rule, underline, link; and the trailing-node feature if StarterKit has it, because it adds an empty paragraph to the end of every document that would then be saved into notes; if you keep it, say so under Choices). `UniqueID.configure({ types: BLOCK_TYPES, attributeName: "id", generateID: () => crypto.randomUUID() })`.
- `taskBlock.ts`: a custom node, not Tiptap's task list wrapper. Group `block`, content `inline*`, one attribute `checked` (boolean, default false). It renders a checkbox before the text and toggling it changes `checked` as one undo step. Enter at the end of a task starts another task; Enter on an empty task turns it into a paragraph.
- Marks: bold, italic, strikethrough and inline code, with Tiptap's stock keyboard shortcuts.
- `ids.ts`: pure `ensureUniqueIds(doc)` that returns the document with an id on every block in `BLOCK_TYPES` that has none and a new id for every repeated one (the first keeps its id). Found while testing: `UniqueID` does not repair the content passed to the editor at load, so loading must go through this function; the save guard stays as the second line.
- `NoteEditor.tsx`: React component with props `doc` (Tiptap JSON) and `onChange(doc)`, using `useEditor` and `EditorContent` from `@tiptap/react`. It does no file access. Minimal styling in `src/editor/editor.css` (no outline on focus, readable spacing, checkbox aligned with the text, works in light and dark). Do not mount it in the app yet; T10.2 does.

**Tests (Vitest, no DOM):**
- Schema check with `getSchema(extensions)`: every block-level node (and `listItem`) is in `BLOCK_TYPES` and has an `id` attribute; the check fails when a node is added to the extensions without being listed; inline nodes such as the hard break have no `id`.
- `ensureUniqueIds`: missing ids filled, repeats replaced, first keeps its id, nested blocks included, inline content untouched.
- A document with an unchecked task, a checked task and each of the four marks survives `Node.fromJSON(schema, doc).toJSON()` unchanged.

**Out of scope:** date chip (later), table, slash menu (T12), drag handle (T17), links, saving.

**Not testable here:** that blocks typed in the app get ids (UniqueID does it at runtime); list it under Not tested, the Mac check covers it later.
done: Schema test covers every block-level node and fails if one is missing from `BLOCK_TYPES` or lacks an `id`; inline nodes have none
`ensureUniqueIds` gives every block a unique id and keeps the first of a repeated one
Checked and unchecked tasks and each text mark survive the schema round trip unchanged
`npm run check` passes

T10.1.title: Document-to-blocks mapping (with T10.2)
T10.1.what:
Convert between the editor document and note blocks, and open and save a note in the editor. Built **together with T10.2 (#35) in one pull request** that says `Closes #34, closes #35`. No new dependencies, no change to the note format. Builds on T09 (#31/#32, merged first).

## Brief

**The format** (from the decision record): a note is a header line, then one block per line: `{"id","type","parent","attrs"?,"content"?}`. Every block-level node is one block with its own id. `parent` is the id of the block it sits in (or `null`); a block and its children are contiguous lines in order. Inline content (text, marks, hard breaks) stays in the block's `content`. Container blocks (`bulletList`, `orderedList`, `listItem`, `blockquote`) have no `content`; their children are the lines that follow. The note files must keep their exact existing shape: use `serializeNote`/`parseNote` and the `Block` type in `src/core/note-format/`.

**Where:** `src/editor/doc-blocks.ts` (pure) and tests next to it; `src/editor/note-io.ts` for open and save over the `Host`; wire it into `src/app/App.tsx` minimally.

**Mapping (`doc-blocks.ts`):**
1. `docToBlocks(doc)` and `blocksToDoc(blocks)`, both using the node names in `BLOCK_TYPES` (`src/editor/blocks.ts`). `id` comes from the node's `id` attribute; other attributes go to `attrs`, and an attribute equal to its schema default is left out (read defaults from `getSchema`) so a note that was not edited re-saves to identical bytes.
2. Loading runs `ensureUniqueIds` (from T09) on the document before it reaches the editor.
3. **A note is only editable if every block is fully understood:** known `type`, keys only from `id, type, parent, attrs, content`, and `attrs` only with attributes the node declares. A note with anything else (a block type from a newer app, extra fields) opens **read-only with a notice** and is never written. Same for a note the scan or parser flagged (skipped lines, newer version, damaged); the existing rule "damaged notes are never rewritten" stands.

**Open and save (`note-io.ts`):**
- `openNote(host, path)`: `loadNote`, then `{ editable, doc, notice }` as above.
- `saveDoc(host, path, loaded, doc)`: new note = the loaded header unchanged (unknown header fields kept) + `docToBlocks(doc)`, saved with `saveNote` so the save guard applies. If the guard refuses, nothing is written and the problems come back for the screen to show. The title is not edited here (T19).
- In `App.tsx`: clicking a note in the list opens it in `NoteEditor` below the list, with a plain Save button and Cmd+S. T11 replaces the button with autosave. Show the notice for read-only notes and the guard's problems for refused saves.

**Tests (Vitest, `MemoryHost`):**
- A fixture with every block type, a nested list (a list inside a list item) and every mark maps both ways with ids unchanged; `docToBlocks(blocksToDoc(blocks))` equals the blocks.
- A 1,000-block document maps back unchanged.
- Save then reload gives an equal document and the same ids; re-saving an unedited note gives identical bytes.
- A refused save (duplicate or missing id) leaves the file's bytes untouched and returns the problems.
- A note with an unknown block type, an unknown field, a skipped line or a newer version opens read-only and a save attempt does not write.

**Out of scope:** autosave (T11), title edits and rename (T19, T07.1), folders, the new layout (T19).

**Not tested:** how the editor looks in the real window (the screenshot check shows it).
done: Every block type and nesting maps both ways; a 1,000-block document maps back unchanged
Save then reload gives an equal document with the same ids; an unedited note re-saves to identical bytes
A save refused by the guard leaves the file untouched and is reported on screen
A note with anything the editor does not fully understand opens read-only and is never written
`npm run check` passes

T11.1.title: Autosave timing and flush on quit (with T11.2)
T11.1.what:
Autosave with a visible state, and save when you leave. Built **together with T11.2 (#38) in one pull request** that says `Closes #37, closes #38`. No new dependencies. Builds on T10 (#34/#35, merged first).

## Brief

**Behavior:** save about 650 ms after the last edit, and immediately on losing focus, switching notes, the window being hidden, and quitting. A failed save never discards an edit: the edits stay in memory, a persistent "not saved" state shows until a save succeeds, and saving is retried.

**Where:** `src/editor/autosave.ts` (pure, no React, timers injectable so tests use fake time) and its test; a small status component beside the editor; `src/host/` for the quit hook; wire into `App.tsx`.

**Controller:** `createAutosave({ save, delayMs = 650 })` with `change(doc)`, `flush()`, `retry()` and `subscribe(listener)`.
- States: `saved`, `dirty`, `saving`, `failed(reason)`.
- Changes within the delay become one save of the latest document. Only one save runs at a time; an edit during a save triggers another save afterward with the latest document.
- `flush()` saves now if there is anything unsaved and resolves when done (also resolves if there was nothing to save); it reports whether the last save succeeded.
- A failed save goes to `failed`, keeps the document, retries by itself (2 s, 5 s, 15 s, then every 30 s) and on `retry()`; success returns to `saved`.
- The save function is `saveDoc` from T10, so the save guard still applies; a guard refusal is a `failed` state with its message, not a retry loop that hides it.

**Quit:** add `onCloseRequested(handler)` to the `Host` interface (`src/host/host.ts`): the handler runs (and is awaited) before the window closes. `MemoryHost` records it and gets `simulateClose()` for tests; the Tauri host uses the window close-requested event (prevent the close, run the handler, then close). If the window needs a permission added in `src-tauri/capabilities/`, add it (no Rust code should be needed; the Rust checks must still pass). If the flush on quit fails, keep the window open and show the not-saved state; a second close request closes it (list this under Choices).

**Screen:** a one-line status near the editor with `role="status"`: "Saved", "Saving…", "Not saved. Retrying…" with a Retry button. The failed state is clearly visible (color and text, not color alone). Remove the Save button from T10.2 or keep it as "Save now" calling `flush()`.

**Tests (Vitest, fake timers, `MemoryHost`):**
- Two changes within 650 ms make one save with the latest document; one change saves after 650 ms.
- `flush()` saves immediately and waits; with nothing pending it does nothing.
- An edit during an in-flight save is saved afterward, none lost.
- A host whose `writeText` fails: the document stays, state is `failed`, a later success returns to `saved`, and the saved file has the edit.
- Quit during a pending delay (`simulateClose()`) saves first; quit with a failing save does not close.

**Out of scope:** the changed-on-disk check (T11.3): until it exists, edit a vault from one place at a time.

**Not tested:** blur, hidden-window and real Mac quit behavior (check on the Mac).
done: Changes within 650 ms become one save; edits during a save are saved afterward, none lost
Quitting during a pending save flushes first
A failing host keeps the edits, shows "not saved" until a save succeeds, and retries
`npm run check` and the Rust checks pass

T19.1.title: App layout and note view (with T19.2)
T19.1.what:
The real window: a note list beside the note, a title field above the editor, new note, and reopening where you left off. Built **together with T19.2 (#57) in one pull request** that says `Closes #56, closes #57`. No new dependencies. Builds on T10 and T11 (merged first) and T07.1 (#25, rename).

## Brief

**Where:** `src/app/` (App, a small `app.css` replacing the inline styles), tests for the pure parts next to them.

**Layout:**
- Left sidebar: the vault name, the note list (title, sorted by title ignoring case; read-only notes marked), a **New note** button and **Choose vault…**.
- Main pane: a title field above `NoteEditor`; the status line from T11.
- Selecting a note flushes the current one first (T11 `flush()`); if that flush fails, stay on the current note and show the not-saved state.
- Simple, calm styling that follows light and dark system settings; usable at the app's default window size and a narrow one.

**Title and rename:** editing the title saves the header title through the same autosave path as the body; once saved, the file is renamed with `renameNote` from T07.1 (`src/core/notes/rename.ts`), and the list and the open path update. A failed rename keeps the title and shows the notice T07.1 returns. Read-only notes have a read-only title.

**New note and reopen (T19.2):** New note creates "Untitled" (`createNote`), selects it and focuses the title. The last vault already reopens at launch (#132/#133): keep that working. Also reopen the last note: remember its path wherever the host already keeps the last vault; if there is no such place, open the first note in the list. A missing remembered note is not an error.

**Tests (Vitest, `MemoryHost`):** a fixture note shows its exact title and every block in order (through `blocksToDoc`); create, edit, quit (`simulateClose()`), reopen keeps the edit; a title change renames the file and keeps `noteId` and content; switching notes with a failing save stays put; sorting ignores case; the remembered note missing falls back to the first.

**Out of scope:** folders (T18), properties, tags, search, trash screen, read-only mode details (T19.3).

**Not tested:** appearance on the Mac (the screenshot check posts it).
done: Opening a fixture note shows its exact title and every block in order
Create, edit, quit, reopen keeps the edit
Editing the title renames the file and keeps `noteId` and content
The last vault and the last note reopen at launch
`npm run check` passes
